subject: Gravity Labs, Entrepreneur in Residence: the first seven weeks

future_perfect.text: By the end of week 7, Gravity will have a pass record where every no carries a dated reopen signal, and one wedge memo that went to committee on a test written before it.
By Friday, Gravity will have two things it can check, each dated, each with what would reopen it.

strategic.text: Work one step after the memo: did each call hold up?

operational.text: Give every pass a dated note of what would reopen it, so a recheck is a test, not a reread.

tactical.text: Day 1: each "no right now" on the pass list gets the signal that would reopen it.

surgical.text: Day 5: a one-page agent-payments wedge memo: no chargeback, freeze on legal process, nothing records what the agent expected.

kairos.fork: Does the pass list reach me on day 1?

premises.text: Gravity keeps a pass list I can read on day 1.
premises.falsifier: No list exists, or it lives only in people's heads.

premises.text: Each pass was written with a reason, not only a no.
premises.falsifier: Most rows carry no reason, so there is nothing to attach a reopen signal to.

kairos.if_true: Reopen signals go on every pass by day 2.
kairos.if_false: Rebuild the list from one conversation; day 1 work slides to day 3 and the memo keeps its day.
kairos.keep_if: The list arrives with a reason on most rows.
kairos.kill_if: No list by day 3: stop waiting and rebuild it from one conversation.

onramp.text: Ask for the list in the first meeting, framed as onboarding, not audit.

offramp.text: Switch to the rebuilt list; the memo keeps its day 5 date.

kairos.fork: Does the agent-payments wedge survive its own memo?

premises.text: The three gaps (no chargeback, freeze on legal process, no record of what the agent expected) are still open on day 5.
premises.falsifier: A card network or issuer publishes agent dispute rights before day 5.

premises.text: Someone at Gravity reads a one-pager in week one.
premises.falsifier: No reply or comment on the memo by the end of the week.

kairos.if_true: The memo goes forward as the first one-pager in the EIR tab's 30-day plan.
kairos.if_false: The kill is written down with its reason, and it becomes the first entry in the pass record.
kairos.keep_if: The three gaps are still open and someone reads the memo.
kairos.kill_if: A network publishes agent dispute rights, or the memo cannot name one buyer.

onramp.text: Write the kill criteria on day 2, before drafting.

offramp.text: Kill it in writing; the reasons become the first pass-record entry.

kairos.fork: Does Gravity send me one idea it passed on?

premises.text: One line, with no names, is enough to rebuild the call.
premises.falsifier: The line names a sector but no reason, and I cannot write a test for it.

kairos.if_true: In two weeks it comes back as keep, kill or not yet, with the dated test that settles it.
kairos.if_false: Nothing to return in week 3; the pass list from K1 is the only test bed.
kairos.keep_if: One passed idea arrives by Friday.
kairos.kill_if: Nothing by Friday: drop the ask from week 2 and use the K1 list.

onramp.text: Ask at the end of the Friday update, one line, no names.

offramp.text: No follow-up chase; the offer stands on the page.

orders.text: Every pass carries a dated reopen signal.

children.text: A recheck becomes a test: the signal fired or it did not.
The team rereads fewer old memos.
A passed idea comes back when its signal fires, not when someone remembers it.
The pass record becomes a source of hatches, rechecked as the market moves.

orders.text: A wedge memo on agent payments exists by day 5.

children.text: The committee can keep or kill it on a named test.
A kill is cheap because the kill criteria were written first.
The next memo starts from the kill record, not a blank page.
The found-or-walk decision in the 180-day plan rests on dated tests, not taste.

best.path: The pass list arrives on day 1, both deliverables land by Friday, and Gravity sends one passed idea.

premortem.cause: Gravity reads the list as an audit of its judgment and holds it back.
The memo's gaps are already closed.
premortem.falsifier: A day-5 search finds no agent dispute rule.

best.postmortem: It worked because the reopen signals were dated, so nobody had to argue about taste.

roi.text: Two checkable things plus a live test bed for week 3.

best.opportunity_cost: Little: the week goes where the plan said.

stop_loss.trigger: The memo cannot name one buyer.
stop_loss.keeps: The pass list with reopen signals.

base.path: A partial pass list arrives by day 3, the memo lands on day 5, and no passed idea comes back yet.

premortem.cause: The list lives in several places.
premortem.falsifier: One owner can name where it is on day 1.
Two blocks of four hours stay clear on the calendar.

base.postmortem: It held because the memo kept its date when the list slipped.

roi.text: The memo lands; the pass list is partial.

base.opportunity_cost: Two days spent finding the list instead of working it.

worst.path: No pass list in week one; only the memo lands, and it reads as a category survey, not a wedge.

premortem.cause: Access to the list needs approvals that take longer than a week.
The memo widens to cover the whole sector.
premortem.falsifier: The memo still names one buyer and one missing record.

worst.postmortem: It failed because the memo had no kill rule written first, so it could not lose.

roi.text: A week spent on access and a memo that reads as a survey.

worst.opportunity_cost: Week 2 starts without a test bed.

stop_loss.keeps: The kill criteria, written on day 2.

derisk.method: List every "no right now" with its stated reason.
Date each reopen signal; drop any signal that has no date.
Write the memo's kill criteria before the memo.
derisk.source: EIR tab, 30/90/180 plan: 30 days, kill criteria written first

derisk.method: Check the memo's three gaps against the pass list: does a passed idea already cover one?
Run a pre-mortem on each branch, each cause with its falsifier.
Friday written update: what held, what moved, what reopens.
derisk.source: EIR tab, 30/90/180 plan: 30 days, a short weekly written update
